function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is an official authorization or instruction that gives someone the authority to act on behalf of another party. In practice, it can refer to:

| Context | What the mandate means |
|---------|------------------------|
| **Legal / Government** | A formal directive from a higher authority (e.g., a court order, a legislative mandate) that requires certain actions or sets rules. |
| **Business / Corporate** | An agreement where one party (the principal) authorizes another (the agent) to perform specific tasks—often seen in procurement, project management, or outsourcing. |
| **Financial / Investment** | A standing instruction that allows a financial institution or advisor to manage assets, execute trades, or handle payments on behalf of a client. |
| **Political** | A mandate from voters or a governing body that empowers a leader or party to implement policies. |

In short, a mandate grants permission and responsibility to act, usually under defined conditions and with accountability to the authorizing entity.
